info.title: LisekMovie
info.description: Main binary: Axum routing, middleware, startup.

post.summary:
Runs the hardware survey with the saved playback settings (FFmpeg
path, balancing) and returns it. Takes a few seconds.

put.summary:
Saves the transcoding pool from the "Sprzęt i Transkodowanie" panel.
Running sessions keep their device; new ones use the new pool.

get.summary:
Every item in one library, for the Admin Panel's browse view that opens
the metadata editor (see `lisek_db::MediaItemSummary`'s own doc comment
for exactly what rides along).

A library's saved custom provider order for one item type
(`"movie"`/`"episode"`) — the Admin Panel's drag-and-drop reordering UI.
An empty `provider_order` (never saved, or explicitly cleared) means
"use the admin's global priority order" — see `apply_provider_order`.

parameters.name: item_type
parameters.description: movie | episode

put.summary:
Nudges one library up or down in the shared display order — the "W
górę"/"W dół" buttons the libraries tab asked for (Runda 9). See
`lisek_db::move_library`'s own doc comment for exactly what "up"/"down"
do (a swap with the immediate neighbor, not a full reorder) and why this
ordering is global rather than per-account.

post.summary:
Queues a scan of one library. Returns the job immediately (202); an
already pending scan of the same library is returned instead of a
second one. Follow progress via `GET /api/admin/scan-jobs/{id}` or the
`scan_progress` events on `/api/notifications/socket`.

get.summary:
Every item currently flagged `metadata_fallback` — the Admin Panel's
warning view.

One item's full editable shape, for the metadata editor to load when
it opens.

put.summary:
The metadata editor's save action — see `lisek_db::update_media_item`'s
own doc comment for why this is the one write in the whole admin
surface that's never gated on `locked_fields` (an admin's own edit
always applies) and the one place `locked_fields` itself, plus
`metadata_locked`/`forced_provider`, actually get written.

post.summary:
The fallback warning view's "Przenieś do folderu mediów" action: copies
whichever of this item's poster/backdrop currently only exist in the
local `config_dir` cache into its media folder (right next to the
video file, same `poster.jpg`/`backdrop.jpg` naming
`metadata_enrichment::enrich_item_cached` already uses), then clears
`metadata_fallback` once at least one image actually made it across —
a partial success (say, the destination folder only just got its write
permission fixed for one of the two files) still counts as real
progress worth reflecting in the flag.

Throws an item's thumbnails away and queues it again (after replacing a
file in place, or to retry a failure).

put.summary:
Sets a provider's API key. Deliberately has no matching "get the current
key" endpoint — [`list_providers`]'s `is_configured` flag is the only
thing a client ever learns about a stored key without setting a new one.

get.summary: The 50 most recent scan jobs, newest first.

get.summary:
How far thumbnail generation has got: totals, per library, the item in
progress and recent failures. The admin page polls it.
Accounts that browse with restrictions (the user list marks them).

put.summary:
Replaces an account's restrictions. `libraries: null` allows every
library, `max_age_rating: null` removes the age limit; both null clears
the restrictions. Takes effect on the account's next request.

post.summary:
Failed attempts are limited per client address and per username (see
`rate_limit`); a blocked client gets 429 with `Retry-After` before any
password hashing happens.

429.description: Too many failed attempts; see Retry-After

get.summary:
Also answers for a session that still has to change its temporary
password, so the client can show the password form.

post.summary:
Accepts a restricted session (temporary password) — that is how the
temporary password gets replaced. Wrong current passwords are limited
per account (`rate_limit::MAX_PASSWORD_CHANGE_FAILURES` per window).

get.summary:
Everything the home page needs in one round trip — see `lisek-db`'s
`get_hero_item`/`list_recently_added`/`list_top_today`/
`list_recommended`/`list_popular` doc comments for exactly what each row
means and, for `top10`/`recommended`/`popular`, the honest placeholder
ranking each uses in the absence of any real watch-history/popularity
tracking (not yet built — see the roadmap).

Every configured library, in the admin's shared display order — the
Navbar's data source (Runda 9), and how the `/library/[id]` grid's own
"which library is this" title/name gets resolved. Public, same as every
other route in this module; reads through the exact same
`lisek_db::list_libraries` (`ORDER BY sort_order, name`) that
`admin::list_libraries` already used for the Admin Panel — one query,
two response shapes, so the Navbar can never disagree with the admin's
own reorder buttons about which library comes first.

Collections with two or more films in this library, by name — the
"Kolekcje" row of a library page.

One page of one library's browsable contents — the `/library/[id]`
page's "all items" grid data source. Runda 9 introduced this endpoint as
a flat, unpaginated, 500-item-capped fetch; Runda 10 adds real
pagination, sorting and an optional starts-with-letter filter (see
`lisek_db::list_items_by_library_page`/`count_items_by_library`), and
changes the response shape to carry `total`/`page`/`page_size` alongside
`items` so the frontend can render a "1–100 z 765"-style counter and
prev/next controls without a second request. This is a breaking change
to last round's response shape; `library_items` had no other known
caller besides this exact page, so changing it in place (rather than
versioning the route) is safe.
get.description:
Bundles the library's own name/type alongside its items in one response
so the page can render its title without a second round trip. A library
id that doesn't exist (deleted, or simply wrong) is a real 404
([`MediaError::LibraryNotFound`]) — unlike [`media_item_seasons`]'s
empty-array contract, there's a meaningful difference here between "this
library exists and has nothing in it yet" and "this library doesn't
exist", and the frontend needs to tell those apart to show the right
message.

get.summary:
The alpha picker's jump table (Faza 12) for one library's "all items"
grid: where each letter's first title sits in the list, for the same
sort and collection grouping. Accented capitals count as their base
letter (Ł under L).

`/library/[id]`'s "Popularne teraz" row — `lisek_db::list_popular` scoped
to this library. Same honest "no real popularity tracking yet" caveat as
the home feed's own popular row.

`/library/[id]`'s "Ostatnio dodane" row — `lisek_db::list_recently_added`
scoped to this library, reusing the exact same query (and therefore the
exact same `home_candidates` grouping and `created_at DESC` ordering) the
home feed's own "recently added" row already uses.

`/library/[id]`'s "Polecane dla Ciebie" row — `lisek_db::list_recommended`
scoped to this library, so a Filmy library never recommends a series and
vice versa. Same honest "no real taste model yet" caveat as the home
feed's own recommended row.

One item's full detail — the "Movie Detail View" the admin asked for
once cards became clickable. Public (any signed-in account, not just
admins — see this module's own doc comment), and deliberately reuses
[`MediaItemResponse`] rather than a bespoke type: the home feed already
carries everything this view shows (title/year/overview/season/episode
plus every image URL), so a separate response shape would just be the
same fields under different names. A dedicated route exists at all
because the home feed only ever returns a handful of rows — an item
reached by direct link (or simply not among the home feed's most-recent
picks) still needs to be fetchable on its own.
Same as [`poster_image`] for the backdrop image.
A chapter's thumbnail (JPEG), made on the first request.

The collection a film belongs to, with its other films (the detail
page's "Z kolekcji" row). 204 when it belongs to none.
The original file as an attachment; supports HTTP Range (resume).

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: From `POST /api/media/{item_id}/download-ticket`.

post.summary: A download URL for an item's original file.
Pin the right provider entry on a film or a whole series ("Fix match").

get.summary: Same as [`poster_image`] for the transparent title-logo image — `.png` media-folder filename and `image/png` content type, matching `lisek_metadata::image_cache::logo_cache_path`'s own `.png` convention (see that function's doc comment for why: real transparency, and every logo this app downloads has already been filtered to PNG at the provider layer). A 404 here just means this item has no logo — a very common, unremarkable case (most titles don't have one cataloged, and TVDB-only items never will yet — see `lisek_plugin_api::ProviderMatch`'s own doc comment), which is exactly why the frontend treats it the same as a missing poster: an `` fallback, not an error state.

The next episode of the same series in season/episode order (a double
episode `E01-E02` is followed by `E03`, a second copy of an episode is
skipped, specials only follow specials). 204 for a movie or the last
episode — see `lisek_db::episodes::next_episode`.

The cast and crew of a film or series (a series card's id is one of its
episodes; every episode carries the series' credits).

parameters.name: transcode
parameters.description: Deprecated: use force_transcode

requestBody.description: Optional; an empty body plays the default tracks

get.summary: Serves one item's poster. `AuthUser` accepts a `?token=` query param specifically so a plain `` can hit this route — see `auth.rs::token_from_query`'s doc comment.

The "Sezony" section's own data — every season, and every season's
episodes, for the show `item_id` resolves to. Public, same as every
other route in this module; an empty array (not a 404) for an id that
doesn't exist, isn't a `media_items` row, or names a movie — see
`lisek_db::list_series_seasons`'s own doc comment on why that's the
right response rather than a distinct error case here.

A season's poster: `<series folder>/seasonNN-poster.jpg`, the local
cache, else the series poster.

put.summary: Watched and/or favourite for every episode of the season (this viewer).

get.summary:
An episode's thumbnail (16:9): the provider's still, a frame cut from
the file, else the series backdrop.

Preview thumbnails of an item; 404 `trickplay_not_ready` until the
background job has made them.

One sheet (JPEG). Cached by the browser for good: its URL changes when
the set is regenerated.

101.description: WebSocket. First frame: JSON {token:string}. Server sends ready, then library_changed with items; administrators also receive scan_progress with the full scan job. Requires an active login; closes when revoked.

get.summary:
A person's profile: biography, dates, links and the titles of this
server crediting them.
A person's profile photo (`?token=` works, as for posters).

End of the period (RFC 3339), default now. A bot run at midnight

401.description: No admin session and no valid X-Lisek-Stats-Key

get.summary:
Always reachable, in every server mode — this is the first thing the
frontend calls on every page load to decide whether to redirect to
`/setup`.

404.description: The session is not the caller's, has ended or expired

index.description: ffprobe stream index: `audio_stream_index` of the playback request.

devices.description: Devices new transcodes are spread over, with their load.

nvenc_available.description: A test frame encoded with `h264_nvenc` on the configured GPU.

tonemapping_backends.description:
Tone mapping backends usable with this build and hardware, fastest
first. `auto` takes the first one.

vulkan_available.description: A Vulkan device opens, so `libplacebo` can tone map on the GPU.

title.description: The file's own chapter name; `None` for numbered or generated ones.

ClientCapabilities.description:
Decoding abilities of one client. Codec names are FFmpeg codec names;
a `_10bit` suffix adds 10-bit decoding of that codec.

containers.description: Containers played from a plain URL: `mp4`, `webm`, `mkv`, `ts`.

interlaced.description: Deinterlaces by itself (TVs do; browsers show combing).

max_audio_channels.description:
Channels the client outputs without downmixing (2 for most
browsers, 6 or 8 with a surround setup).

max_width.description:
Picture size worth sending when re-encoding (the screen), 0 for no
limit.

CollectionResponse.description: One collection with its films in release order.

CreditResponse.description: One person credited on an item.

CrewMember.description: A director or writer, linking to their page.

dropoff.description: Abandoned sessions per tenth of the title (index 0: 0–10 %).

DatabaseConfig.description:
Discrete connection fields, as collected by the First-Run Wizard form.
Kept separate from a raw connection-string type so the wizard never has
to build (or the frontend parse) a `postgres://` URL by hand.

DayStats.description: Viewing per calendar day in `timezone` (an IANA name PostgreSQL knows).

video_copied.description: The video stream is passed through untouched.

configured.description:
In the configured set (a device just removed from the pool may
still finish sessions).

transcodes.description: LisekMovie sessions on it now (starting ones included).

url.description: Open this URL (no header needed) to download.

DownmixPreference.description: What the client asked for. `Auto` lets the server choose.

device.description: GPU index or render node the test ran on.

error.description: Last line FFmpeg printed when the test failed.

runtime_minutes.description: The file's length, else the provider's runtime.

title.description: The provider's title; `None` before enrichment ("Odcinek N").

FallbackItem.description:
Every item currently flagged `metadata_fallback` — the Admin Panel's
warning view (see the Faza 5-completion roadmap item) lists these with
a "move to the media folder" action per row, so the admin doesn't have
to `SELECT` the database by hand to find out which items only ever got
their poster/backdrop into the local cache. `file_path` rides along so
the caller (`lisek-server`) can derive the exact media-folder
destination the same way `metadata_enrichment::media_folder_destination`
already does, without a second lookup.

hardware_encoders.description: Hardware encoders compiled into this build.

hwaccels.description: `ffmpeg -hwaccels`: hardware decoding methods in this build.

FilmographyItemResponse.description: One title of a person's filmography.

oneOf.description: Required unless the server already has a database (`DATABASE_URL`).

active_transcodes.description: LisekMovie transcodes on this GPU now.

encoder_sessions.description: NVENC sessions of every process on this card.

index.description: `nvidia-smi` index (NVIDIA only): the number transcodes use.

HardwareDevice.description: One transcoding device of the pool (Faza 14).

decode_codecs.description: Source codecs this device decodes (empty: decoding on the CPU).

device.description:
`nvenc`: the `nvidia-smi` index (`0`). `qsv`/`vaapi` on Linux: the
render node (`/dev/dri/renderD128`); `qsv` on Windows: the DirectX
adapter number or `auto`.

encode_codecs.description: Output codecs it encodes (`h264`, `hevc`; empty: CPU encoding).

max_sessions.description:
Most sessions at once on this device; 0 = no limit. A full pool
transcodes on the CPU.

name.description: Shown in the admin panel (from the diagnostics).

weight.description:
Share of sessions, 1–16: a device with 2 gets twice the sessions
of one with 1 before both are equally loaded.

pool_candidates.description:
Devices the transcoding pool could use (Faza 14), from this survey:
NVIDIA cards (NVENC), Intel GPUs (Quick Sync, else VA-API), AMD GPUs
on Linux (VA-API); codecs from the tests and `vainfo`. Suggestions:
`enabled` is off, the admin panel merges them with the saved pool.

warnings.description:
Things worth the administrator's attention, as codes:
`no_hardware_encoder`, `nvenc_failed`, `acceleration_off`,
`nvidia_smi_missing`, `other_encoders_unused`, `ffmpeg_missing`.

balancing.description: Live: devices transcodes are spread over and their load.

pool.description: The saved pool (Faza 14), also when no diagnostics ran yet.

oneOf.description: The latest diagnostics since the server started, if any.

HourStats.description: Viewing per hour of the day (0–23) in `timezone`: when people watch.

provider_id.description: The provider's id of the right film or series (from the search).

image_saved.description: At least one new image was saved.

items_updated.description: Films or episodes updated (a series counts every episode).

chapters_generated.description:
`true` when the file has no chapters and `chapters` are evenly
spaced scenes instead.

default_audio_index.description: The audio stream played when none is picked.

external_links.description: IMDb, TheTVDB, TMDB, in that order, when the item has those ids.

original_title.description: Shown under the title when it differs from it.

runtime_minutes.description: Length of the file (or of an episode, from the provider).

oneOf.description:
Streams of the file (films; a series card's representative episode
has its own). `None` until the file was probed.

items.description: Directors, writers, then the cast in billing order.

index.description:
0-based position of the letter's first card in the unfiltered
list: page `index / page_size + 1`, card `index % page_size`.

letter.description: `A`..`Z`, or `#` for titles starting with anything else.

letters.description: Letters with at least one card, in list order.

LibraryRowResponse.description:
Response shape shared by [`library_recent`]/[`library_recommended`]/
[`library_popular`] (Runda 10) — deliberately identical to
[`LibraryItemsResponse`]'s `library`+`items` fields minus the pagination
ones, since these three are small curated rows, not a paginated grid.
Each of the three handlers independently looks up the library (rather
than sharing one earlier lookup) so a failure in one section's request
can never take another section down with it — see the Runda 10 plan's
reasoning for three separate endpoints instead of one bundled response.

client.description:
Free-text identity for the `sessions` table (a future "your active
sessions" screen), never validated against anything — absent fields
just fall back to "unknown".

MediaItemDetail.description:
One item's full editable shape — what the metadata editor loads and
what it hands back for [`update_media_item`]. `original_title` reads
straight from `metadata->>'original_title'` (see the Faza
5-completion migration's doc comment for why that's a JSONB key, not a
column) and `overview` from the same `provider_data` slot the home feed
already reads (a manual edit and a provider match both land there —
see [`update_media_item`]). `locked_fields` names, verbatim, whichever
of `"title"`/`"original_title"`/`"year"`/`"overview"` the admin has
individually protected — the same identifiers the editor's own
checkboxes use, so the frontend never needs a translation table.

age_rating.description:
An administrator's own age rating (parental controls), which wins
over the provider's. `None`: the provider's value applies.

provider_age_rating.description: What the provider says (shown next to the override in the editor).

MediaItemResponse.description: One item as the frontend consumes it: `lisek_core::MediaItem` plus its image URLs, which aren't stored anywhere — they're just this item's id slotted into the routes below. Always present, even for an item with no cached image of that kind yet; the routes themselves 404 rather than this struct trying to know in advance whether a file exists on disk — mirrors the poster/backdrop `` pattern already established on the frontend (see `MediaCard.svelte`/`HeroBanner.svelte`), which `logo_url` reuses as-is: a card or the Detail View just tries loading it and falls back to the plain text title if that 404s, exactly like a missing poster falls back to nothing. `item_type` is `"movie"` or `"series"` as of Runda 8 — never a bare `"episode"` any more (see `lisek_db`'s `home_candidates` CTE doc comment): every response this module hands out already represents something browsable on its own, not one file out of a season.

age_rating.description:
Detail view only: minimum viewer age (parental controls) and the
certification it comes from, e.g. 13 and "PG-13". A rating set by
an administrator has no certification.

badge.description:
`"new_series"` / `"new_season"` / `"new_episodes"` for a `"series"`
row (see `lisek_db::classify_series_badge`'s doc comment), or
`"new_movie"` for a `"movie"` row added within
`lisek_db::RECENT_BADGE_DAYS` (Runda 9 — see [`is_recently_added`]),
or `None`. Only ever set by [`to_response`], for whichever row it's
given; the plain [`From`] impl below always leaves it `None`, which
is what [`media_item_detail`] (the single-item Detail View endpoint)
returns as-is — the badge is a browse-card affordance (home feed,
and as of Runda 9 the `/library/[id]` grid too — both go through
[`to_response`]/[`to_responses`]), not something the Detail View
itself was ever asked to show.

item_count.description:
`"collection"` cards only: how many of its films this card stands
for.

MediaItemSummary.description:
Every item in one library, for the Admin Panel's browse view that opens
the metadata editor — deliberately not paginated yet (a self-hosted
library's realistic size doesn't need it at Faza 5's scope; revisit if
that stops being true). `metadata_locked`/`metadata_fallback` ride
along so the browse list itself can show a lock/warning badge without a
second request per row.

direction.description:
`"up"` or `"down"` — anything else is [`AdminError::InvalidInput`],
same validate-before-any-query discipline as [`create_library`]'s
own `library_type` check.

MyAccessResponse.description: What the signed-in account may do beyond browsing.

restricted.description: Parental controls limit what this account sees.

key.description: Shown once; only its hash is stored. Send it as `X-Lisek-Stats-Key`.

NextEpisodeResponse.description: The episode a player offers when one ends ("Następny odcinek").

title.description: Series title (episodes carry no title of their own yet).

filmography.description: Titles in this server's libraries the account can see, newest first.

role.description:
`"Actor"`, `"Director"` or `"Writer"`: what they are best known
for here.

buffered_seconds.description: Media buffered ahead of the position.

stalls.description: Rebuffering since the previous report (not counting seeks).

allow_remux.description: Copy a compatible video stream into HLS instead of re-encoding it.

downmix_algorithm.description:
Default stereo downmix of surround audio: `standard` (ITU-R
BS.775), `dialogue` (louder centre channel), `night` (dialogue plus
dynamic range compression) or `pro_logic_ii` (matrix-encoded for
receivers that decode Dolby Pro Logic II).

gpu_load_balancing.description:
Share GPU transcodes between several NVIDIA GPUs (Faza 13): each new
session goes to the card with the fewest sessions (then the most
free memory). Off: every session uses `hardware_device_index`.

hardware_device_index.description:
GPU used for decoding, filtering and encoding (CUDA device order,
see `nvidia-smi -L`).

hardware_device_path.description:
Device for `qsv` / `vaapi` (Faza 14): a Linux render node
(`/dev/dri/renderD128`), on Windows a DirectX adapter number (`0`)
or `auto` (Quick Sync only). Empty: `/dev/dri/renderD128` / `auto`.

hardware_devices.description:
GPUs to share between (`nvidia-smi` indices). Empty: every GPU
`nvidia-smi` reports, or `hardware_device_index` without it.

hardware_encode_codecs.description:
Output codecs the hardware encoder may produce (`h264`, `hevc`);
others are encoded on the CPU.

hardware_pool.description:
Transcoding devices of `hardware_acceleration = "pool"` (Faza 14):
NVIDIA, Intel and AMD GPUs side by side, each with its share of
sessions and the codecs it decodes and encodes.

hevc_encoding.description:
Encode HEVC instead of H.264 for clients that decode HEVC (NVENC
only). Same quality at a lower bitrate.

hls_segment_seconds.description:
HLS segment length when the video is re-encoded, in seconds. A
copied video is cut at its own keyframes, close to this length.

max_concurrent_transcodes.description: Simultaneous video encodes. Remuxes (copied video) do not count.

segment_retention_seconds.description: Segments further than this behind the player are deleted.

subtitle_fallback_charset.description:
Character set of external text subtitles that are not UTF-8 (Polish
`.srt` files are usually Windows-1250).

throttling.description:
Pause FFmpeg once it is this many seconds ahead of the segment the
player last asked for, and resume it at half of that. Until then
FFmpeg runs at full speed, so playback and seeking start at once.

tonemapping_backend.description:
Where HDR -> SDR tone mapping runs: `auto` picks the fastest one the
FFmpeg build supports (`cuda` > `libplacebo` > `opencl` >
`software`). `cuda` needs jellyfin-ffmpeg's `tonemap_cuda`.

devices.description: The whole pool as the admin panel shows it (enabled and disabled).

use_pool.description:
Transcode with the pool (`hardware_acceleration = "pool"`). Off:
back to the CPU when the pool was in use; other modes stay.

ProgressAck.description: What the server answers a report with.

resume_position_seconds.description: Where playback resumes next time (0 = from the start).

watched.description: The item now counts as watched.

ProgressEvent.description:
Why the player sent a report. Heartbeats arrive on a timer; the
others when the state changes, so the stored position is never more
than one heartbeat behind.

ProgressRequest.description: The older per-session endpoint, kept for clients built against it.

ended.description: The viewer left (not: played to the end).

failures.description: Providers whose search failed (network, rejected key).

results.description: Candidates of every provider asked, each provider's best first.

PublicLibraryResponse.description:
One library as the Navbar/`/library/[id]` grid consume it — deliberately
thinner than `admin::LibraryResponse`: `root_paths` are absolute
filesystem paths on the machine the server runs on, and have no business
reaching a non-admin browser tab (Runda 9). Every signed-in account gets
to see *that* a library exists and what the admin named it, never where
its files actually live.

block_unrated.description: With an age limit, also hide items that have no rating at all.

can_download.description: The account may download original files (`GET /api/media/{id}/download`).

libraries.description:
`None`: every library. `Some`: only these (an empty list hides the
whole catalog).

max_age_rating.description: Items rated above this minimum age are hidden. `None`: no limit.

ScanJob.description: One scan, as stored and as reported to clients (HTTP and WebSocket).

ScanPhase.description: Documents the values of [`ScanJob::phase`] in the API schema.

ScanStatus.description:
Documents the values of [`ScanJob::status`] in the API schema (the
column itself is plain text, constrained by a CHECK).

favorite.description: Every episode is one of the viewer's favourites.

name.description:
The provider's name ("Sezon 1", "Odcinki specjalne"); `None` before
enrichment.

play_id.description: The episode "Play" opens: the first one not watched yet.

poster_url.description: Always set: the season's own poster, else the series poster.

SeriesEpisodeResponse.description:
One episode, as the "Sezony" section renders it — see
`lisek_db::list_series_seasons`'s doc comment for exactly why this is
this thin (no title/thumbnail/runtime/overview: none of it exists
anywhere in this app yet). `poster_url`/`backdrop_url` reuse the exact
same `/api/media/{id}/...` routes as [`MediaItemResponse`] — `id` here
is a real `media_items` row, so they resolve the same way.

SessionQuality.description: One playback session as the admin quality view shows it.

active.description: Reported within the last two minutes and not ended.

SessionRow.description: One session in the dashboard's list.

duration_seconds.description: 0 when the player never reported a length.

position_seconds.description: Where the viewer was last (stopped, for an abandoned session).

Slice.description: One slice of a breakdown (platform, device type, content type).

audio_stream_index.description: ffprobe index of the audio stream (see `audio_tracks`).

burn_subtitle.description:
Burn the subtitle into the picture even when it is text (keeps ASS
styling; costs a transcode). Picture subtitles are always burnt.

oneOf.description:
What the client decodes. Omitted: the preset of its browser/TV
family, recognised from the User-Agent.

start_position_seconds.description: Start here instead of at the saved resume position.

subtitle.description:
Subtitle track id from `subtitle_tracks`: `s<index>` embedded,
`x<n>` a file next to the video.

stream_url.description: The file (direct play) or the HLS master playlist.

time_offset_seconds.description: Always 0 now: HLS playlists cover the whole file.

label.description: "14.09 - 20.09" for a week, "20.09" for a day, in `timezone`.

id.description:
`subtitle` of the playback request: `s<index>` embedded, `x<n>` a
file next to the video.

kind.description: `"text"` or `"image"` (image subtitles are burnt into the picture).

external.description: A file next to the video rather than a stream inside it.

hls_rendition.description:
Position among the HLS subtitle renditions (hls.js
`subtitleTracks`), for switching without restarting playback.

url.description: WebVTT for a `<track>` element (direct play only).

TitleRank.description: A film or a series in a ranking.

id.description: The film, or the series' representative item: `/media/{id}`.

series_id.description: The series itself (series rankings only): filter value.

TrickplayFailure.description: A failed item for the admin list.

TrickplayManifest.description:
What a player needs to show previews: tile geometry and sheet URLs.
Thumbnail `n` (the moment `n * interval_seconds`) is on sheet
`n / (columns * rows)`, column `n % columns`, row
`(n % (columns * rows)) / columns`.

count.description: Thumbnails in total (the last sheet may be partly empty).

sheets.description: Sheet image URLs in order; like other images they take `?token=`.

failed.description: Generation failed for the current file (retried once it changes).

pending.description: Still waiting: no thumbnails yet, or made from an older file.

ready.description: Thumbnails made from the current file.

average_seconds.description: Average seconds per item over the latest generations (since start).

oneOf.description: The item being generated right now.

ffmpeg_missing.description: FFmpeg could not be started (check Admin → Playback).

paused_for_playback.description: Generation waits because someone is transcoding.

age_rating.description:
Faza 6: the administrator's own age rating (minimum viewer age,
0–21) for parental controls; `null` or absent leaves the
provider's rating in charge.

User.description:
A local account. Never carries the password hash — that stays inside the
db/auth layers and must never be serialized back to a client.

Deliberately has no sqlx dependency or derive: lisek-db maps database rows
onto this struct field by field, so this crate stays free of any notion
of Postgres or SQL (see the architecture plan's crate boundaries).

enforced.description: `false` for an administrator: administrators always see everything.

UserRestrictionsResponse.description:
An account's access restrictions (parental controls) as the admin
editor shows them.

VaapiDevice.description: VA-API capabilities of one render node (`vainfo`).

VideoSummary.description: The picture, as one line ("4K HEVC HDR").

lisek_auth.name: Authorization
lisek_auth.description: LisekMovie Client="web", Device="Browser", DeviceId="...", Version="1.0.0-beta", Token="..."
